solution.title: Application Packaging & Deployment Standards (Win32, MSIX & Store) — Org-Wide Specification & Quality Gates

products.name: Application Packaging & Deployment Standards (Win32, MSIX & Store) — Commercial
products.short_description: The org-wide standard that keeps your Intune app catalog consistent, auditable, and clean at scale — a mandatory naming/version/metadata convention, a format decision tree (Win32 vs MSIX vs Microsoft Store vs legacy LOB), detection-rule standards with 10 banned patterns, five package quality gates, a peer-review sign-off process, assignment-hygiene rules, and five Graph audit scripts. The specification layer above per-app packaging.
products.description:
Stop your app catalog from decaying — set the standard, then audit it

An app catalog decays predictably. The first ten apps are fine because one person built them all. By app forty there are three naming styles, detection rules only one person understands, apps assigned to groups nobody can explain, several apps with no owner, and a Test - do not use app that has been pushed to every device for months. Nobody did anything wrong — there was simply no standard. The cost is real: failed installs nobody can triage, licence spend on software still deployed to leavers, audit findings because there's no record of what was approved, and a “don't touch that app” culture where the safest move is to build a duplicate.

This solution is the organisation-wide packaging specification that prevents that decay. It sits above the mechanics of packaging any single app — it does not re-teach how to wrap a .intunewin. It governs how every application is named, formatted, detected, documented, reviewed, released, and audited across your whole tenant, for years.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the standard as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can adopt end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell that audits your live catalog.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every tenant object you create is named once and reused verbatim through the templates, the gates, and the audit scripts.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable governance engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Adopt once, reuse on every package forever.
  • Tested — a pilot-first model (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates, so no package reaches broad release without a signed sign-off record.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — the standards layer, its four control points (intake, build, release, operate), the three delivery formats you govern (Win32, MSIX, Microsoft Store) plus the legacy LOB/MSI type being retired, and exactly what the standard produces.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (a named standard owner, two reviewers, the Graph SDK and scopes, packager-vs-approver RBAC, a retained-evidence document store, a real pilot population, the Government-cloud Microsoft Store position, an agreed category taxonomy, and a baseline audit) with how to verify and implement each.
  • Implementation Guide — stand up the tenant objects, then the specification itself: a format decision tree and matrix, the naming / version-stamping / metadata standard, the detection-rule acceptability rules and ten banned patterns, the install / uninstall command, return-code, and reboot standards, a reusable Package Intake & Specification template, a five-gate acceptance checklist, a peer-review and sign-off process with retained evidence, ring and assignment-hygiene rules, and an enforcement and audit cadence (baseline, monthly, quarterly, annual) with an exceptions register.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts (Microsoft Graph) — a package-standard compliance auditor, a detection-rule quality checker that flags the ten banned patterns, an assignment-hygiene reporter (orphans, All-Devices targeting, Required+Uninstall conflicts, duplicates, missing exclusion), a metadata-completeness scorer, and a preview-by-default metadata remediation tool that changes nothing without an explicit apply.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates — validating both that the standard is in place and that a package passes cleanly through it.

Scoped to avoid overlap

This is deliberately the standards layer. If you also need the hands-on mechanics of packaging a single application — the Content Prep Tool, install/uninstall commands, authoring one detection rule, supersedence — that is a separate, complementary discipline. This product governs the org-wide standard; it does not duplicate per-app packaging.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each rollout feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook across every package, every team, and every audit cycle.

The bottom line

An app catalog that a new starter can pick up in days, an auditor can answer questions about in minutes, and a growing team can extend without it becoming a liability — because the standard, the templates, the quality gates, and the audit scripts are all in place from the first package onward.

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse across unlimited packages.
